paper.title: Transcriptional Suppression of Six Critical Biosynthetic Enzyme Genes Contributes to Disruption of Aflatoxin Production in Aspergillus oryzae XJ-1, a Locust Biological Control Agent
paper.authors: Hu S, Xu X, Wang F, Li J, Du J, Fu J, You Y, Zhang L.
paper.association_evidence: Europe PMC record PPR1329704. The abstract names the same four strains as the BioProject (A. oryzae XJ-1 and CGMCC 3.9544, A. flavus CGMCC 3.3950 and 3.4408) and a transcriptome analysis of aflatoxin genes; the last author (Long Zhang) is the BioSample collected_by. The full text (data availability statement) returned HTTP 403, so no accession-level link was seen.

study_summary.objective: Explain why the locust biocontrol strain A. oryzae XJ-1 produces no aflatoxin, by comparing aflatoxin-gene transcription with non-aflatoxigenic and aflatoxigenic strains.
study_summary.experimental_design: RNA-seq of A. oryzae XJ-1 and CGMCC 3.9544 in potato dextrose broth, three parallel samples each; the project also has A. flavus CGMCC 3.3950 and 3.4408 runs, not imported. Culture time and temperature not stated.
study_summary.main_finding: Per the preprint abstract: XJ-1 carries all 22 aflatoxin-cluster genes but transcribes six biosynthetic genes (avnA, verB, omtA, ordA, vbs, cypX) much less than aflatoxigenic A. flavus.

broth culture; shaken or static not stated
